title: Tune a heat exchanger deliberately
equipment: Plate heat exchanger with four independent simulated controller copies
physicalPurpose: Choose a heat-exchanger PI tuning from declared accuracy, response, and valve-use requirements rather than from one formula.
principalTechnique: Staged manual PI tuning and historical ultimate-cycle tuning comparison
objective: Tune proportional and integral action one term at a time, reproduce a historical critical-cycle PI tuning, and select the least aggressive candidate that satisfies the declared requirements.

simplifications: Each controller drives an independent copy of the same local FOPDT plant
Flow, inlet temperatures, heat-transfer coefficient, valve dynamics, and fouling are fixed
The common load is represented by a minus-1-degC equilibrium shift on the two PI copies

baseline.limitation: Proportional-only control retains offset, while the first deliberately slow integral setting does not recover from the common load inside the declared time.

change.decision: Prefer the least aggressive candidate that meets final accuracy and overshoot requirements while retaining every failed trial and actuator-use trade-off.

disturbances: A minus-1-degC equilibrium-temperature load at 100 s on the manual and historical PI copies
Independent deterministic 0.05-degC measurement noise on all copies

acceptance.window: sample at 180 s in the separately compiled Ki=0.05 trial
between equivalent alternating peaks after 10 s
between equivalent alternating peaks after 10 s
sample at 180 s after the common load
sample at 180 s after the common load
10 to 180 s divided by manual PI total variation over the same window

abortPredicates: Any required sample or timing value is nonfinite or has invalid quality
Any measured outlet temperature leaves 40 through 60 degC
Any applied valve position leaves 0 through 100 percent
The plant, initial state, sample interval, seed, noise, event, or limit differs between compared candidates
safety.restorationMode: Restore the reviewed common setpoint to 50 degC and observe every simulated copy return toward its 20-percent equilibrium command
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised process controls engineer and heat-exchanger operator
simulationOnlyRestrictions: The critical-cycle and tuning evidence in this lesson cannot authorise a physical experiment or gain application
Physical tuning requires independently reviewed topology, process hazards, operating window, interlocks, personnel, immediate experiment approval, and separate validation

video.viewerOutcome: Tune one heat-exchanger PI deliberately and explain why a much faster historical candidate is not automatically better.

learning.context: Four independent copies of the same locally validated plate heat exchanger compare manual proportional-only, manual PI, critical proportional-only, and historical PI control.
learning.reason: A validated plant model does not choose the acceptable compromise among response speed, overshoot, disturbance rejection, robustness, and valve movement.
theory: Bias supplies the equilibrium command, proportional action responds to present error, integral action accumulates past error, and derivative action responds to measured rate.
Manual tuning changes one term at a time and adds a term only when measured evidence justifies it.
Ultimate gain and ultimate period describe one declared critical experiment, while the historical Ziegler-Nichols PI rule embeds an aggressive quarter-decay objective.
Requested and applied commands differ when actuator limits intervene, so saturation and applied valve movement are retained separately.
learning.workedPrediction: Predict 1.25 degC manual-P offset, rejection of Ki=0.05 at 180 s, an accepted Ki=0.10 manual candidate, critical Ku 22.24 and Pu 11.35 s, and historical PI Kp 10.01, Ti 9.46 s, Ki 1.06 with much greater valve travel.
practicalPreparation: Verify Simulation evidence, accepted local model scope, four independent plants, signals, units, gains, bias, limits, quality, 100 ms timing, noise, seed, events, and restoration.
Record predictions, equivalent run conditions, metric equations, windows, validity rules, and decision thresholds before enabling the common setpoint step.
learning.baseline: Manual proportional control retains predictable offset, and the first deliberately slow Ki=0.05 trial fails the declared post-load recovery requirement.
learning.change: Raise only manual integral gain to 0.10 and separately calculate a historical PI candidate from the measured critical gain and period.
learning.comparison: Compare equivalent runs using settled late error, rise time, overshoot, settling status, load IAE, peak valve position, saturation, and cumulative applied-valve total variation.
learning.validation: Require both PI candidates to reach at most 0.10 degC final error, manual overshoot at most 5 percent, measured critical period from 9 to 14 s, formula agreement within 0.02, and historical valve travel at least twice manual travel.
learning.explanation: The manual tuning is slower and less active because it accumulates integral correction conservatively; the historical tuning is faster and valve-intensive because it inherits an aggressive critical-cycle objective.
learning.transfer: Select the least aggressive controller that meets declared requirements; Lesson 43 estimates the critical point with a bounded relay experiment while retaining review and explicit application boundaries.
